title: Distributed Workflow Orchestration Engine with Event Sourcing, Saga Compensation & Crash Recovery
problem: Multi-step distributed business processes (e-commerce order fulfillment, fintech loan origination, cross-service media transcoding) span heterogeneous microservices that fail unpredictably due to network partitions, database deadlocks, and worker node crashes. Ad-hoc script orchestrators and point-to-point HTTP integrations lack crash-safe state checkpointing, resulting in orphaned tasks, duplicated financial activities, and inability to rollback distributed state upon partial failure. This project builds a durable, distributed workflow orchestration engine in Go inspired by Temporal and Conductor. The engine models workflows as deterministic state machines, records execution history via PostgreSQL event sourcing, distributes activity execution over Kafka worker queues, guarantees deterministic replay upon process restart, executes automated Saga compensation handlers on failure, and exposes a management REST API with sub-900ms crash recovery.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Multi-Step Order Fulfillment & Inventory Reservation
use_cases.first_sentence: E-commerce platforms executing checkout pipelines involving inventory reservations, payment authorizations, and warehouse dispatch must guarantee end-to-end consistency.
use_cases.second_sentence: The Go workflow engine orchestrates multi-step activities; if payment authorization fails, the engine triggers automated compensating actions to release reserved warehouse inventory.

use_cases.title: FinTech Multi-Tier Loan Origination & KYC Verification Pipeline
use_cases.first_sentence: Digital lending applications requiring asynchronous credit bureau checks, document identity verifications, and underwriting approvals can stall across days.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine checkpoints workflow progress into PostgreSQL event stores, waking hibernating workflows deterministically upon asynchronous webhook receipt.

use_cases.title: Distributed Cloud Media Transcoding & Video Pipeline Orchestration
use_cases.first_sentence: Video processing platforms ingesting raw 4K footage must divide files into chunks, execute parallel GPU encoding tasks, and assemble master HLS manifests.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine schedules parallel activities across Kafka worker pools, monitoring task heartbeats and automatically re-queuing dropped tasks upon worker node crashes.

hard_parts: Designing a deterministic workflow history replayer in Go that reconstructs in-memory execution state from append-only PostgreSQL event streams
Implementing backward Saga compensation workflows that trigger compensating activities in reverse execution order upon downstream failures
Guaranteeing exactly-once activity execution semantics using Kafka message keys, worker heartbeats, and idempotent task completion tokens
Handling worker process crashes (SIGKILL) mid-workflow and recovering execution state within sub-second recovery bounds
screener_signals: Clean Go codebase cleanly separating workflow definitions, state machine history replayer, event sourcing persistence, and Kafka worker dispatchers
High-concurrency benchmark report proving sustained execution of 1,200+ concurrent workflow activities per second with sub-50ms latency
Anti-fake verification script killing a worker node mid-workflow at step 3, asserting heartbeat timeout detection, state recovery, and successful completion

architecture.data_flow: A client submits a workflow via REST API; the coordinator writes WorkflowStarted to PostgreSQL; the decision engine determines the first activity and publishes an ActivityTask to Kafka; a worker polls Kafka, executes the activity, and sends ActivityCompleted with results; the coordinator appends the event to PostgreSQL and evaluates the next step; if an unrecoverable failure occurs at step 3, the Saga compensation controller is invoked; it traverses history backwards and dispatches compensating tasks (CompensateStep2, CompensateStep1) to Kafka; upon worker crash, a secondary worker re-reads event history from PostgreSQL, reconstructs state, and resumes execution without re-executing completed activities; Prometheus scrapes workflow metrics.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Deterministic event sourcing replay checks verifying state parity before dispatching activities, with PostgreSQL version row locks.

targets.report: Workflow execution benchmark report and task processing latency log

targets.metric: Deterministic Process Crash Recovery Replay Duration

targets.input: Worker killed at step 3 of a 5-step workflow with 10 historical events stored in PostgreSQL
targets.environment: Go workflow coordinator running with 500ms heartbeat timeout monitoring
targets.minimum_pass: State reconstruction and activity resumption completes in < 1.2 seconds with 0 state corruption
targets.target: State reconstruction and activity resumption completes in < 650 milliseconds with 0 state corruption
targets.report: Crash recovery event timing log and deterministic replay audit summary

targets.metric: Saga Backward Compensation Rollback Parity Rate
targets.method: Percentage of simulated workflow failures triggering exact reverse-order execution of all compensating activities
targets.input: 50 synthetic workflows programmed to fail at step 3, requiring compensation for steps 1 and 2
targets.environment: Kafka worker pool configured with automated Saga compensation handlers
targets.minimum_pass: 50 of 50 failed workflows execute compensation in exact reverse order with 0 orphaned resources
targets.target: 50 of 50 failed workflows execute compensation in exact reverse order with 0 orphaned resources
targets.report: Saga compensation execution audit log and reverse activity sequence trace

riskiest_component.name: Non-Deterministic Execution Divergence during Event History Replay
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce strict determinism linter forbidding system clock calls, random number generators, or external I/O inside workflow logic.
riskiest_component.fallback: Workflow execution quarantine marking divergent runs for manual operator inspection with audit snapshots.

rubric.expected_result: Replay verifies steps 1 and 2 read from PostgreSQL event store; only steps 3, 4, and 5 dispatch to workers
rubric.evidence_location: Dynamic verification console execution output log
rubric.pass_criterion: Console confirms exactly 0 duplicate activity executions during recovery with exit code 0

worksheet.q5: Hard parts: deterministic event history replayer, backward Saga compensation, exactly-once activity execution, and crash recovery.
